title: A river town decides, a harbour counts, and a bridge reopens
summary: Synthetic content for reviewing the premium layout only. Every place, number, person and event in this edition is invented; it is not a researched Daily Board.

edition.thesis: Three invented stories, each set in the component that explains it best.

stories.title: Ribera votes on Sunday. The count, not the debate, decides it.
stories.label: Region · vote 25 October
stories.dek: Two fictional candidates closed their campaigns level. Polls close at 17:00 and the first official count follows the same evening.
stories.whyItMatters: Ribera's port handles a large share of the fictional region's exports, so its next council sets fees that reach well beyond the town.
stories.whatsNext: Polls open at 08:00. The electoral board publishes its first partial count after 19:00.

disagreement.label: Room for disagreement
disagreement.text: Supporters of the challenger argue the polls undercount new residents, who registered late. If so, the race is less even than it looks.

sources.title: Electoral board: Sunday's vote, times and candidates
sources.note: Invented official notice used to demonstrate source cards.

sources.title: Final debate: fees, housing and the port
sources.note: Invented independent report. Polls described there are not results.

blocks.text: The two candidates met for a final debate on Friday and argued mainly about port fees and housing. Neither landed a clear blow, and both now say the turnout of new residents will decide the race.
Where the race stands before the vote.

items.label: First partial count
items.text: The board publishes counted tables as they arrive.

blocks.text: The same race, read three ways.

tabs.label: What happened
tabs.text: A final debate with no decisive moment, and polls that put the candidates within a point and a half of each other.

tabs.label: Why it matters
tabs.text: Port fees set by the next council feed into the price of almost everything shipped from the fictional region.

tabs.label: What to watch
tabs.text: Turnout in the two new riverside districts, where most late registrations came from.

stories.title: The harbour is busier. The town around it is not, yet.
stories.label: Economy · September data
stories.dek: Cargo through the invented port rose for a fifth month, while shop sales in town fell from a year earlier.
stories.whyItMatters: A strong port and a weak high street can coexist. Reading only one of them gives a misleading picture of the local economy.

sources.title: Retail survey, September
sources.note: Invented survey of 140 shops; small sample.

blocks.text: Shop sales compared with a year earlier
Two honest readings of the same month.

items.label: The port's month
items.text: Cargo up 19% on a year earlier, driven by grain.

items.label: The high street's month
items.text: Most shop categories sold less than a year ago.

blocks.title: Still unknown
blocks.text: Whether port wages are reaching town shops at all. The survey does not ask where customers work.

stories.title: The old bridge reopens with a lighter deck
stories.label: Local · works finished 23 October
stories.dek: After fourteen months of work, the invented Ribera bridge carries traffic again, with a weight limit for lorries.
stories.whyItMatters: Commutes across the river shorten by about twenty minutes for most of the east bank.

blocks.text: We rebuilt the deck to carry less weight for much longer. Lorries over twelve tonnes will use the ring road.
blocks.speaker: A. Medina

items.label: Closed
items.text: Cracks found in the deck supports.

items.label: Reopened
items.text: Cars, buses and bicycles; lorries limited.

items.label: Load review
items.text: Engineers review the weight limit after winter.

blocks.text: Why a lighter deck lasts longer.
steps: Every crossing flexes the deck a little; the supports absorb that load.
A lighter deck means less of the load is the bridge carrying itself.
Less constant load leaves more margin for traffic, so the supports tire more slowly.

stories.title: The riverside market moves to evenings for summer
stories.label: Local · from 1 November
stories.dek: Stalls open 18:00 to 23:00 from November to February, the invented market board says.
